newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says to sign oil contract with China soon.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says to sign oil contract with China soon.

text.p: A Chinese technical delegation was in Baghdad and Iraq hoped to sign an oil development contract with China very soon, Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said on Friday.
"I hope the contract with the Chinese will be signed very soon, sooner than expected," Rasheed said at a news conference in Baghdad.
The delegation from the China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) will soon be accompanied by a high-level group led by Chinese ministry officials, officials at the Iraqi oil ministry said.
China is interested in the development of the billion barrel Ahdab field in southern Iraq. Officials also said China had eyes set on the prized Halfaya field in the south.
Rasheed said negotiations with the Chinese were "at a very advanced stage." So were talks with the French and Italians, he said.
Halfaya was discovered 20 years ago and is believed to hold commercial reserves of about five billion barrels, the official said.
Iraq believes the field could produce some 250,000 barrels a day (bpd) at full capacity.
Talks, the minister said, were going on smoothly with Italy's Agip SpA which also was mentioned in connection with Halfaya. Rasheed was in Italy last month to pursue talks with Agip.
French Elf Aquitaine and Total have agreed in principle with Iraq to sign for development respectively of the Majnoon and Nahr Umar fields once sanctions are lifted.
In March three Russian companies secured the rights to develop eight billion barrels of Iraqi reserves held in the giant southern Qurana field.
Russia's LUKoil has a majority 52.5 percent stake with two other Russian companies holding 22.5 percent between them and Iraq 25 percent.
Iraq has been encouraging potential oil production partners to sign upstream agreements despite a U.N. ban on investment which will postpone the lion's share of any work until sanctions are lifted.
Investment in Iraq is banned under the U.N. embargo imposed after Iraq's invasion of Kuwait in August 1990.
Rasheed said Iraq had drawn up plans to boost its oil production up to six million barrels per day once sanctions on it are lifted.
